about: LAB-2063 (HP EV-3, G2): what each Start-here benchmark is made of, reviewed by hand against the installed inspect_evals 0.27 sources and the benchmark's paper. `roof eval anatomy` reads the rest from the benchmark's own files and leaves out what it cannot read. Also holds each benchmark's marking sentence and lesson line for Explore › Questions (LAB-2064; {target} is the question's reference answer). Keys are inspect_evals folders.

mmlu_pro.marking: Code reads the letter after ANSWER: and compares it with {target}. No model is involved.
mmlu_pro.lesson: Ten options, not four: guessing gets 10 %, so 40 % is far above chance.
watch_out: Scores from other frameworks often use a different prompt or few-shot examples.

gpqa.maker: Rein et al., New York University
gpqa.marking: Code reads the letter after ANSWER: and compares it with {target}. No model is involved.
gpqa.lesson: 198 questions: one more right answer moves the score half a point, and the 95 % range is wide.
watch_out: Experts in the field reach about 70 % (the paper); recent models score higher.

hle.maker: Center for AI Safety & Scale AI
hle.marking: A grader model reads the final answer and the reference ({target}) and says whether they mean the same. Same meaning in different words still counts.
hle.lesson: When every model scores near the floor, the 95 % range matters more than the ranking.
watch_out: The judge is a second model, so it costs extra and can be wrong.
The questions are public now, so a model trained after release may have seen them.

steps.title: Prompt
steps.body: System asks for an explanation, then Answer: and a confidence.

steps.title: Model answers
steps.body: Explanation, then Answer: and Confidence: lines.

steps.title: Judge compares
steps.body: A grader model checks the final answer against the reference. Same meaning in different words still counts.

steps.title: Two numbers
steps.body: Accuracy, plus calibration error: is a 70 % confidence right 70 % of the time?

simpleqa.marking: A grader model compares the answer with {target}: correct, incorrect, or not attempted.
simpleqa.lesson: Saying 'I don't know' is not attempted, which is better than a wrong answer.
watch_out: Abstaining is allowed: compare correct and attempted-correct, not just one number.

truthfulqa.marking: Code compares the chosen option with {target}. No model is involved.
truthfulqa.lesson: The popular answer is the wrong one here: bigger models used to score lower.
watch_out: The number of options changes from question to question, so chance varies.

gsm8k.marking: Code reads the number after ANSWER: and compares it with {target}. No model is involved.
gsm8k.lesson: A right answer in the wrong format is wrong here: no ANSWER line scores zero.
watch_out: Most frontier models are above 90 %: GSM8K now separates small models, not big ones.

math.marking: The answer is checked for being the same expression as {target}, by code and by a grader model.
math.lesson: 1/2 and 0.5 are the same answer: equivalence, not string match.

aime2025.marking: Code compares the final integer with {target}. No model is involved.
aime2025.lesson: 30 problems: one more right answer moves the score 3.3 points.
watch_out: Only 30 questions: run several attempts each to narrow the range.

arc.marking: Code reads the letter after ANSWER: and compares it with {target}. No model is involved.
arc.lesson: An older benchmark most frontier models saturate.

bbh.marking: Code compares the final answer with {target}. No model is involved.
bbh.lesson: Chain of thought on or off changes the score a lot.
watch_out: Each task has its own chance level; the average hides it.

musr.marking: Code compares the chosen option with {target}. No model is involved.
musr.lesson: Multi-step reasoning over a long text.

ifeval.marking: Code checks each rule in the prompt (word counts, format, no commas, …). No model is involved.
ifeval.lesson: Strict and loose scoring: a rule half-followed counts in loose only.
watch_out: Rules are about form, not quality: a useless answer can pass.

humaneval.marking: The function runs against the benchmark's unit tests in a sandbox. No model is involved.
humaneval.lesson: pass@1 is what the model usually does; pass@k what it can do.
watch_out: Saturated for frontier models; the code really runs, so Docker is needed.

mbpp.marking: The code runs against the task's assert tests in a sandbox. No model is involved.
mbpp.lesson: Compare with HumanEval: the same skill should give a similar ranking.

bigcodebench.marking: The code runs against the task's tests in a sandbox. No model is involved.
bigcodebench.lesson: Real libraries make it much harder than HumanEval.

livecodebench_pro.marking: The program runs against hidden test cases in a sandbox. No model is involved.
livecodebench_pro.lesson: Problems dated after training: memorisation vs skill.

swe_bench.marking: The patch is applied and the repository's own tests run in a sandbox. No model is involved.
swe_bench.lesson: The agent around the model matters as much as the model.
watch_out: Each question is a container: slow and heavy on a laptop.

bfcl.marking: Code checks the call: function name, arguments and their types. No model is involved.
bfcl.lesson: Exactly right or wrong: a call with one bad argument fails.

tau2.marking: Code checks the final state of the simulated database and the policy steps.
tau2.lesson: A simulated customer talks back: the run uses a second model as the customer.
watch_out: The simulated customer is a model too, so it costs extra and varies.

gaia.marking: Code compares the final answer with {target} after normalising it. No model is involved.
gaia.lesson: One exact answer at the end of many steps: the web and files along the way.

niah.made_of: A fact hidden in long text
niah.marking: A grader model checks whether the answer gives the hidden fact.
niah.lesson: Score by where the needle sits and how long the haystack is, not one number.

xstest.marking: A grader model says whether the answer complied, refused, or partly refused.
xstest.lesson: Over-refusal: refusing a safe question is a failure too.

strong_reject.marking: A grader model rates how much the answer helps with the harmful request.
strong_reject.lesson: Under-refusal: the other side of XSTest.
